# Publish New Blog Post — Manual Editorial Workflow

**Static template. Do not edit this file when publishing. MJ just provides files + topic; Claude Code derives everything else.**

---

## What MJ Provides Each Time (Outside This File)

Per post, MJ uploads to Claude Code:
- **Topic / title** of the blog (e.g., "Best Website Development for Small Businesses in Toronto 2026")
- **`content.md`** — primary article source
- **`content.html`** — fallback for tables and complex HTML elements
- **`content.docx`** — Word version (rarely needed, included for completeness)
- **Featured image** — file or URL
- **Inline images** — files or URLs with brief description of each

That's it. MJ does NOT edit this template. Everything below is static.

---

## Claude Code: Your Job

Read this entire file before doing anything else. Then read all files MJ provided. Then build the Sanity blogPost document manually using editorial judgment. Land it at `status='ready-for-review'`. Report the Studio URL.

**Do NOT:**
- Call `enrich-arvow-post.ts`, `parseMarkdown()`, or any function from `src/lib/post-transformer/`
- Modify the Astro template or Sanity schema
- Auto-publish (status must stay `ready-for-review`)
- Touch any existing published post
- Auto-create new categories (ask MJ first)

**Do:**
- Use editorial judgment, not regex patterns
- Match the gold-standard structure (see Step 1)
- Derive slug, category, internal links, entities from the article content
- Output a structured final report

---

## Step 1 — Read the Gold-Standard Reference

Fetch the Sanity blogPost with slug `how-to-make-landing-page-design-work-in-2026-budget-guide`. Read the full document including `body` Portable Text array and all schema fields. Study:
- Body block count and density (~25–35 blocks for a typical 1,500–2,000 word article)
- Position and frequency of `statCallout` blocks (1–2 per post, mid-body in data-heavy sections)
- Position of `pullQuote` blocks (1 per post, in left gutter near a strong opinion paragraph)
- H2/H3 hierarchy
- Bulleted list patterns with bolded labels
- `inlineImage` block format (alternating left/right tilt)
- Internal link `markDefs` structure
- Final Recommendation section pattern (names CiCon, includes CTAs)

**This is your structural reference. Match this rhythm. Not identical content — similar density and editorial cadence.**

---

## Step 2 — Read MJ's Inputs

Read `content.md` and `content.html` from the paths MJ provided. Identify:

- **Quick Answer** — usually labeled "Quick Answer" or is the article's first 1–2 paragraphs. Extract clean text, under 400 chars, ending at sentence boundary.
- **Strongest stats** — pick 1–2 for inline `statCallout` blocks. Priority: percentages > dollars > multipliers > timespans. The strongest one (with source attribution) goes to End CTA.
- **Most quotable line** — for `pullQuote`. Look for strong declarative, brand-aligned, conviction-laden sentences. Prefer lines mentioning CiCon, Majid Behzad, or stating a clear principle.
- **Tables** — convert HTML `<table>` to bulleted list with bolded labels per row, OR `comparisonTabs` block if the schema supports it cleanly.
- **6 FAQ Q&A pairs** — extract from `## Frequently Asked Questions` section.
- **Final Recommendation** — usually already CiCon-branded in Arvow articles. Light editorial touch only.
- **Boilerplate to strip:** any `_Last Updated: ..._` lines, duplicate "Quick Answer" labels, bottom WhatsApp/phone CTA paragraphs (template renders its own End CTA), `* * *` horizontal rules, "About the Author" paragraphs at the end (template renders from author reference).

---

## Step 3 — Derive Required Values from Inputs

### Slug
From the topic/title MJ provided. Kebab-case, lowercase, no special characters, max 96 chars. Strip filler words ("the", "a", "for") if needed to keep it focused. Examples:
- "Best Website Development for Small Businesses in Toronto 2026" → `website-development-toronto-small-businesses-2026`
- "Local SEO Guide for Dental Clinics in the GTA" → `local-seo-dental-clinics-gta`

### Category
Read the article topic. Match to one of the existing categories in Sanity:
- **Local SEO** — Google Business Profile, Map Pack, citations, local-keyword content
- **Paid Advertising** — Google Ads, Meta Ads, PPC, campaign management
- **Dental Marketing** — dental clinic specific topics
- **Social Media** — Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, organic social
- **Strategy & Growth** — analytics, conversion, attribution, general digital marketing strategy
- **Web Design & Development** — website development, landing pages, CRO, UI/UX
- **Conversion & CRO** — conversion optimization, A/B testing, landing page strategy

Query Sanity to confirm the category exists:
```typescript
sanityClient.fetch(`*[_type == "blogCategory" && name == $name][0]`, { name: '[chosen]' })
```

If the article doesn't fit any existing category, STOP and ask MJ. Do not auto-create.

### Internal links (2–3 per post)
Identify CiCon service pages relevant to the article topic. Available service pages:
- https://cicon.ca/marketing-services/website-development/
- https://cicon.ca/marketing-services/local-seo-optimization/
- https://cicon.ca/marketing-services/dental-marketing-services/
- https://cicon.ca/marketing-services/paid-advertising-services/
- https://cicon.ca/marketing-services/social-media-marketing-services/
- https://cicon.ca/marketing-services/ai-seo-and-seo/
- https://cicon.ca/marketing-services/crm-integration/
- https://cicon.ca/marketing-services/media-content-production/

Pick 2–3 that thematically fit. Distribute throughout the body (not stacked in one paragraph).

### Author
Always Majid Behzad. Resolve `_id`:
```typescript
sanityClient.fetch(`*[_type == "author" && name == "Majid Behzad"][0]._id`)
```

### Related posts (3)
Query 3 most recent published posts from the same category, plus 1 from a related category if same-category has fewer than 3:
```typescript
sanityClient.fetch(`*[_type == "blogPost" && status == "published" && category._ref == $catId][0...3]`)
```

### Entities (about + mentions)
Read the article body. Identify:
- **About entities (2–3):** the core entities the article is about. Always include CiCon Marketing if relevant. Geographic entities (Toronto, GTA, etc.) if local. Primary topic as a `Thing`.
- **Mentions entities (5–10):** secondary brands, products, organizations, places mentioned. Examples: Shopify, WordPress, Google Analytics 4, Statistics Canada, HubSpot CRM, MaRS Discovery District, Cloudflare, etc.

Each entity:
```typescript
{ _key: uuid(), name: '...', type: 'Thing' | 'Place' | 'Organization' | 'Person', sameAs: 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...' }
```

Default `type: 'Thing'` unless clearly Place/Organization/Person. Use Wikipedia URLs. If no Wikipedia entry exists for an entity, omit it.

### Meta title (55–62 chars) and meta description (130–160 chars)
**Sanity-enforced limits.** Write to fit the range, not the topic.
- metaTitle: typically `[Title] | CiCon Marketing` if under 62 chars, otherwise just `[Title]`
- metaDescription: rephrase the Quick Answer to fit 130–160 chars with primary keyword early

### End CTA stat
Pick the strongest stat from the article. Format:
```typescript
{ number: '48%', context: 'one-sentence context', source: 'Statistics Canada, 2025' }
```

If no strong stat exists, use a CiCon-known fact (e.g., "250+" projects, "14+" years experience).

---

## Step 4 — Build the Sanity Document Manually

Construct a complete `blogPost` document. Build the Portable Text body array block by block.

### Required document structure

```typescript
const newPost = {
  _type: 'blogPost',
  title: '[from MJ]',
  slug: { _type: 'slug', current: '[derived]' },
  dek: '[one-sentence brand-voice dek, 130-160 chars]',
  category: { _type: 'reference', _ref: '[resolved]' },
  author: { _type: 'reference', _ref: '[resolved Majid Behzad _id]' },
  heroImage: {
    _type: 'externalImage',
    url: '[featured image URL from MJ]',
    alt: '[descriptive alt — derive from filename/topic if not provided]',
    caption: null,
    source: 'editor-uploaded'
  },
  readTime: [word count / 225, round up],
  publishedAt: [ISO timestamp now],
  quickAnswer: '[extracted, under 400 chars]',
  body: [
    // Portable Text blocks — see structural rhythm below
  ],
  faqs: [
    // 6 faqItem objects, each with _key (uuid), question, answer
  ],
  endCtaStat: { number: '...', context: '...', source: '...' },
  aboutEntities: [/* 2-3 entities */],
  mentionsEntities: [/* 5-10 entities */],
  relatedPosts: [/* 3 references */],
  metaTitle: '[55-62 chars]',
  metaDescription: '[130-160 chars]',
  keywords: ['primary keyword', 'secondary keyword', 'cicon marketing'],
  status: 'ready-for-review',
  inlineImagesPendingReview: false,
  needsFaqAddition: false,
  enrichmentRequired: false,
  notes: [
    `Manually built by Claude Code on ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
    'Source: provided by MJ as content.md + content.html + images'
  ]
}
```

### Body structural rhythm (match gold-standard)

Target 25–35 body blocks. Pattern:

1. **Intro paragraphs (2–3 blocks)** — value prop + local/topical context. Include 1 internal link.
2. **First H2** — main argument or data section
3. **Paragraph(s) under H2** with one `statCallout` inserted mid-section
4. **`inlineImage` block** (tilt: left)
5. **More paragraphs** continuing the argument
6. **Second H2** — comparison/process/depth section
7. **Bulleted or numbered list** if comparing options (bolded labels per item)
8. **`inlineImage` block** (tilt: right)
9. **Paragraph leading to pullQuote**
10. **`pullQuote` block**
11. **Third H2** — process or framework
12. **Numbered list** if presenting a process
13. **Closing paragraph for that section**
14. **`inlineImage` block** (tilt: left)
15. **Final H2: "Final Recommendation"**
16. **Closing paragraphs** naming CiCon, with 1–2 more internal links

### Block formatting reference

Paragraph:
```typescript
{ _type: 'block', _key: uuid(), style: 'normal', markDefs: [], children: [{ _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: '...', marks: [] }] }
```

Paragraph with bold:
```typescript
{ _type: 'block', _key: uuid(), style: 'normal', markDefs: [],
  children: [
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: 'Normal. ', marks: [] },
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: 'Bold', marks: ['strong'] },
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: ' more.', marks: [] }
  ]
}
```

Paragraph with internal link:
```typescript
{ _type: 'block', _key: uuid(), style: 'normal',
  markDefs: [{ _key: 'k1', _type: 'link', href: 'https://cicon.ca/marketing-services/website-development/' }],
  children: [
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: 'Text with ', marks: [] },
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: 'linked phrase', marks: ['k1'] },
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: ' here.', marks: [] }
  ]
}
```

H2:
```typescript
{ _type: 'block', _key: uuid(), style: 'h2', markDefs: [], children: [{ _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: 'Heading', marks: [] }] }
```

Numbered list item:
```typescript
{ _type: 'block', _key: uuid(), style: 'normal', listItem: 'number', level: 1, markDefs: [],
  children: [
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: 'Step Name:', marks: ['strong'] },
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: ' description.', marks: [] }
  ]
}
```

Bulleted list item:
```typescript
{ _type: 'block', _key: uuid(), style: 'normal', listItem: 'bullet', level: 1, markDefs: [],
  children: [
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: 'Label:', marks: ['strong'] },
    { _type: 'span', _key: uuid(), text: ' description.', marks: [] }
  ]
}
```

statCallout:
```typescript
{ _type: 'statCallout', _key: uuid(), number: '71%', label: 'context', source: 'attribution' }
```

pullQuote:
```typescript
{ _type: 'pullQuote', _key: uuid(), quote: 'The sentence.', attribution: 'Source — context' }
```

inlineImage (external):
```typescript
{
  _type: 'inlineImage', _key: uuid(),
  source: 'external',
  externalUrl: 'https://...',
  alt: 'descriptive alt',
  caption: null,
  tilt: 'left'  // alternate left/right across the article
}
```

faqItem (inside faqs array):
```typescript
{ _key: uuid(), question: 'Question?', answer: 'Answer text.' }
```

---

## Step 5 — Verify Before Writing

Before calling `sanityClient.create()`, output the constructed object to console. Self-check:

- [ ] Body block count: 25–35
- [ ] At least 1 `statCallout` exists
- [ ] At least 1 `pullQuote` exists
- [ ] All inline images present as `inlineImage` blocks (NOT raw markdown text)
- [ ] 2–3 internal CiCon service links exist as `markDefs`
- [ ] `faqs` has exactly 6 items with `_key`, `question`, `answer`
- [ ] `endCtaStat` has `number`, `context`, `source` all populated
- [ ] `metaTitle` length: 55–62 chars
- [ ] `metaDescription` length: 130–160 chars
- [ ] Slug doesn't already exist in Sanity (query first)
- [ ] No body block contains "Last Updated" text
- [ ] No body block contains raw markdown image syntax `![...]`
- [ ] `aboutEntities` has 2–3 items, `mentionsEntities` has 5–10
- [ ] `relatedPosts` has 3 valid references

If any check fails, fix it before writing. If the source article genuinely doesn't support a check (e.g., zero stats for a `statCallout`), use the strongest available content as fallback rather than omitting the block.

---

## Step 6 — Write to Sanity

```typescript
const result = await sanityClient.create(newPost)
console.log('Created:', result._id)
```

---

## When This Workflow Fails

If the output is structurally wrong:
1. Don't republish in a loop — revert status to `ready-for-review` first
2. Diagnose specifically (missing block? wrong field type? component not rendering?)
3. Patch surgically, one issue at a time
4. Add the failure mode to "Known Issues" section below

---

## Known Issues / Lessons Learned

(Add new ones here as encountered.)

- The Astro template renders inline `![...](...)` markdown as text, not images. Always convert to `inlineImage` blocks during Step 4.
- The Final Recommendation section in Arvow articles is usually already CiCon-branded — light editorial touch only.
- Tables from Arvow articles convert better to bulleted lists with bolded labels than to `comparisonTabs` when there are 6+ rows.

- ❌ Pipeline B Arvow webhook → `enrich-arvow-post.ts` auto-enrichment (deprecated May 2026). Code remains in repo for reference only.
